messages.subject: Problems with readTranscriptFeatures function
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I have been workind with methylkit recently but I found one problem with one function of the package genomation related with methylkit. My code is the following:

gene_meth <- readTranscriptFeatures(location = 'genes_v5.bed')

and that returns me the following error:

Reading the table...
Calculating intron coordinates...
Error in .Call2("solve_user_SEW0", start, end, width, PACKAGE = "IRanges") :
  solving row 3671: negative widths are not allowed

I supposed that was some mistake of the strand/end column but I checked that all the columns respect that start < end, so this is not the problem.

The genes_v5.bed file have the following form when I load it with R:

and the row that is giving me the error is:

I can not understand why is giving me this problem if clearly the start column is smaller than the end column. In addition I also remove the information of isoforms in order to avoid name problems.

I would be very thankfull if someone can give me some hint about how to fix this problem with the function readTranscriptFeatures().

messages.subject: see effect of covariate vs effect of treatment (or main factor)
messages.subject_clean: see effect of covariate vs effect of treatment (or main factor)
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I have run Methylkit to compare the metylation levels between 2 groups, so I use a binomial test afterwards. I have introduced a covariate, as my data might have internal structure (samples come from different bee colonies), but they might have not cause I am working with pure genetic lines, so maybe the colony effect here is not relevant. I could not find a way yet to see to what extent (statistically speaking) is worth including my covariate, and how much of the methylation differences is this factor explaining. Could somebody help me there, please?

Kind regards,

messages.subject_clean: [methylkit_discussion] see effect of covariate vs effect of treatment (or main factor)
messages.body_plain:
you can try to run the test with treatment only and treatment+covariate. If the covariate do not have a significant effect (does not explain the variation in methylation levels) you will have the same number of differentially methylated CpGs.

Best,
Altuna
